beats.spoken: Wednesday, 3 p.m. You have an AI chat shorten your quote for a big client. Personal account, done in a minute. Then you click thumbs up, because it did a good job.

So what happens to the chat? Using Claude as the example: for personal accounts like Free, Pro and Max, Anthropic uses chats to improve its models if you allow it. And clicking thumbs up or down counts as feedback. Then Anthropic keeps the whole conversation for up to five years.

fact.text: Feedback keeps the whole conversation for up to five years.

beats.spoken: What do you do? A: It's fine, it's just a quote. B: You switch off training in your personal account and carry on. C: For business data, you use a business account with a contract. Remember your choice.

The right answer is C. For Claude for Work and the API, Anthropic says it doesn't use the data for training, unless a contract says otherwise. So the contract decides, not a switch in the settings. A misses the feedback, B still has no contract.
Contract first, then the chat. Germany's BSI reminds us that generative AI also brings new security risks. What would you have picked? Tell me in the comments.
